items.stem: What is the correct order for registering error-handling middleware in Express?

options.text: After all routes, as the last middleware with four parameters (err, req, res, next)
options.rationale: Correct: Express identifies error middleware by its four-argument signature and it must come last.

options.text: Before any routes so it runs first
options.rationale: Then it would never catch route errors.
A centralised handler avoids duplication and catches forwarded errors.

options.text: It must have exactly two parameters
options.rationale: Error middleware is recognised by its four parameters.

items.explanation: Correct: Express identifies error middleware by its four-argument signature and it must come last.

items.stem: Which HTTP status code best indicates a resource was successfully created?

options.rationale: Correct: 201 signals a new resource was created.
200 is a generic success, less precise for creation.
204 means success with no body, used for deletes/updates.
400 indicates a client error, not success.

items.explanation: Correct: 201 signals a new resource was created.

items.stem: Which practices improve an async Express route handler? (Select TWO)

options.text: Wrap awaited calls so rejected promises are passed to next(err)
options.rationale: Correct: unhandled rejections otherwise crash or hang the request.

options.text: Return appropriate status codes for validation failures
options.rationale: Correct: clear status codes communicate outcomes to clients.

options.text: Perform all database work synchronously to avoid promises
options.rationale: False; blocking the event loop harms throughput.
False; hiding errors as success misleads clients.
